newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares strike back to higher levels.
newsitem.headline: German shares strike back to higher levels.

text.p: The German share market continued its process of recovery on Wednesday from a ten percent drop last week, and advanced to within around one hundred points of its former all-time high in pre-bourse trade.

The IBIS DAX index stood at 3,373.62 points, up 45.49 points or 1.37 percent, boosted chiefly by the strength of the dollar at 1.71 marks. Trade was also underpinned by a stronger overnight close on Wall Street.
"The dollar is the major theme today but the fact that New York seems to be stabilised is also helping," a Frankfurt trader said.
Dealers said comments by Goldman Sachs strategist Abby Joseph Cohen were also supportive.
She said on Tuesday the market correction in the U.S. was over and the Standard & Poor's 500 stock index was likely to end the year at 850, up from its recent record closing high of 816.29.
"Abby Joseph Cohen seems to be calling the shots at the moment, and if she says the market consolidation may be over, then we listen," a Frankfurt trader said.
One of the winners pre-bourse was Fresenius Medical Care (FMC).
Shares in FMC, the dialysis subsidiary of German medical Tuesday's analysts' meeting.
Shares were up 8.90 marks, or six percent, at 157 marks, while the overall IBIS DAX index of electronic trade.
Neither FMC nor its parent Fresenius AG profited much from positive figures on Tuesday, and dealers said there was an element of catch-up in the positive performance in pre-bourse trade.
Fresenius preference shares also outperformed the market, up 10 marks, or 2.78 percent at 370 marks.
"Fresenius and FMC have room for growth, offer innovative products and a good management structure. They will stay on the buy list," a Frankfurt dealer said.
Exporters were lifted by the higher dollar. Daimler-Benz was up two marks, 1.56 percent, at 130.10 marks, while BMW was up 35.40 marks, or 2.63 percent, at 382 marks.

Chemicals were also higher -- Hoechst was up 90 pfennigs, or 1.33 percent, at 68.55 marks, Bayer was up 1.29 percent at 69.80 marks, although BASF AG was lower than its peers, up 0.65 percent, at 66.15 marks.
